entries.en: Tower Collapse Affects Some Radio Stations
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k127; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The collapse of Miyato Sky Tower is expected to affect some radio broadcasts.

Most television and radio stations had moved their transmission equipment to a newly completed broadcast tower, retaining Miyato Sky Tower as a backup, so their broadcasts are unaffected.
However, some radio stations had not relocated and are currently off the air.
There is reportedly no estimate for when broadcasting will resume.

＜Radio stations currently off the air＞
・FM Urashimaso
・Sakura FM

entries.en: Gyaos Fires Mysterious Rays!
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k133; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
We have further news about Gyaos. An individual has reportedly been observed emitting rays from its mouth. These rays are said to cut through whatever they strike.

The government announced that, as the attack uses ultrasound, it will call the rays the 'Ultrasonic Scalpel.'
In response, the Japan Medical Society has protested that the name duplicates that of a surgical instrument.

Whether only certain individuals can emit them or all individuals possess the ability remains unknown. Either way, there can be no doubt that the threat posed by Gyaos has increased.

entries.en: Horrifying Discoveries About Flying Monsters

entries.en:
As we gradually learn more about Gyaos, a truly horrifying fact has emerged.
Gyaos were actually eating one another atop their nest.
Experts suspect they may be able to reproduce and increase their numbers even without food.

entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k137; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
How much do you know about Children's Day?
The Constitution defines Children's Day as follows:

'To respect children's individuality, promote their happiness, and express gratitude to mothers.'

Yes, Children's Day is also a day to thank mothers.
Why not express your gratitude to your parents on Children's Day as well as Mother's Day?

entries.en: Government Secrets: Disguised News Helicopters?
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k139; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
News helicopters flew around Miyato Sky Tower after Gyaos began nesting there.
My independent investigation revealed that these were actually government helicopters disguised as news aircraft, intended to keep Gyaos confined to the nest.
Why the disguise? I suspect it was because the government wanted to protect Gyaos despite knowing that they preyed on humans.
I intend to continue investigating to pursue this suspicion.

entries.en: Helicopter Crashes
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k141; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
A news helicopter covering Miyato Sky Tower crashed after being attacked by Gyaos.
Witnesses say it was approaching the tower when it went down.
If this is true, perhaps Gyaos attacked while the helicopter was trying to rescue people abducted to the nest?
The pilot reportedly had not been authorized to approach the tower.

entries.en: Everything Is 'For the Customers'
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k143; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
We have learned that among those stranded on the first floor after the second floor of Miyato Sky Tower's observation deck was destroyed, a female shop assistant continued selling goods.

Despite vicious Gyaos nearby, she reportedly prioritized sales over her own evacuation.
She said, 'As long as even one person wishes to make a purchase, I cannot leave this place.'
Our reporting indicates she was hired at Miyato Sky Tower a year ago. Several months before that, as graduation approached, she had failed in job applications to hundreds of companies. Then her parents died unexpectedly, and her home burned to the ground in a suspicious fire.
Although neither she nor her parents were at fault, she felt sorry for neighbors affected by the spreading fire. She sold the land where her home had stood, the last thing she owned, and paid them everything.

Having lost everything but the clothes on her back, she sat alone and stunned in a park at dusk.
No tears came. So many misfortunes had struck that she could feel nothing.

Then an elderly man, passing by on a walk, happened to speak to her. Light entered her life again.
He was the founder and chairman of the company operating Miyato Sky Tower.

After hearing her story, the chairman reportedly arranged somewhere for her to live that very day and decided to hire her as a shop assistant at Miyato Sky Tower.
He said he sympathized because he, too, had lost his parents when young and endured great hardship.

Ever since, she had worked with single-minded devotion.
She treasured being alive and having the happiness of a future to think about.
Perhaps precisely because she was such a person, her concern for others was strong enough to keep her serving customers in defiance of this adversity.

entries.en: A Couple
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k145; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
While Gyaos flew overhead, a drama like the one in this footage unfolded on the first floor of Miyato Sky Tower.
A dying man and an injured woman huddle together. Their subsequent whereabouts are unknown.
But a ring worn by the woman has been found on that first-floor observation deck. Am I the only one who finds that troubling?

entries.en:
This is matter regurgitated by Gyaos.
According to someone who escaped from the first floor of Miyato Sky Tower's observation deck, a person was seen sticking a hand into it.
Why that person did so is unknown.
Were they searching for something? Did they enjoy the texture? Or had the overwhelming situation left them completely bewildered?

Meanwhile, a company that noticed its viscosity has reportedly succeeded in developing a shock-absorbing material with similar components. We will report again when more details become available.

entries.en: Why AED Installation Needs Subsidies
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k149; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
You have probably often seen AEDs, now installed at all kinds of facilities.
Since these are provided by the facilities or their management companies, those organizations naturally bear the purchase and maintenance costs.
This is becoming a growing burden. A set like the one pictured costs around 300,000 yen, its battery lasts about four years, and the AED itself has a five-year warranty, requiring replacement or repurchase each time. Furthermore, the battery is not designed for recharging and is basically discarded after one use.

AEDs save lives in emergencies and are extremely important. They should be available in more places. Yet I cannot help questioning why this is left entirely to private goodwill.
This is precisely when the government should take the lead. There is no need to raise taxes. Simply reducing bureaucrats' abnormally high salaries to private-sector levels would provide 500,000 AED sets. Population density would matter, but even a simple calculation suggests more than 100,000 units for each of the 47 prefectures. Wouldn't that be a substantial help, even to an amateur's mind?

Does the government want to protect the people, or its own bureaucrats? That is the question.

entries.en: The Unused Fire Hose
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k151; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The fire-hose equipment installed on Miyato Sky Tower's observation deck was found with no sign of having been used.
Since there had been no fire, that is only natural.

However, some argue that using its high-pressure water against Gyaos might have improved the chances of survival.
I am skeptical. True, I have heard an urban-legend-like story about such a jet bringing down a helicopter, though not Gyaos. But Gyaos is an unknown quantity.
It is entirely possible that this would merely have angered them and caused even greater damage.

So-called pundits excel at finding faults and making negative comments, but they have never truly felt the circumstances on the ground. As someone placed in the same broad category of mass media, I can only regret the prevalence of such people.

entries.en: An Elevator That Brings Happiness?
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k157; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Have you heard the widely whispered rumor that the elevator on the right as you face Miyato Sky Tower brings happiness?
One person says they confessed their love in it and later married. Another lost everything when their company failed, but found a lottery ticket in this elevator. Its owner never came forward, and it won an astonishing one billion yen.

But tracing these rumors revealed something suspicious.
Apparently, a tower employee started the story to attract customers.
It seems to have spread when some of those who rode the elevator because of it claimed, out of vanity, that something good had happened to them.
Of course, I do not mean to deny mysterious powers entirely. But it appears this is not about making its riders happy: it is about making Miyato Sky Tower happy. (Visitor numbers have more than tripled since the rumor began.)

entries.en: An Elevator That Is a Huge Gamble?
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k159; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
The elevator on the left as you face Miyato Sky Tower is called the 'Huge Gamble Elevator.'
When two or fewer people descend in it, a spirit always appears, leaving them psychologically impaired by the time they reach the bottom.
The damage is severe, and very few can return to ordinary life.
However, roughly one in fifty encounters a spirit with a peaceful expression and subsequently enjoys a prosperous life.
Among those I interviewed, some simply received great wealth and now live comfortably. Another suddenly developed a refined sense of taste, pursued the cooking career they had given up on, and now works at the forefront of a famous restaurant overseas.

Nevertheless, because all but a tiny minority suffer what might be called devastating impairment, the elevator was once closed, and at another time a dedicated employee ensured that at least three people descended together.
But many were captivated by the appeal of a secure future if things went well. Now two or fewer may ride if they first sign a document accepting personal responsibility.

Why only when descending? Why two or fewer? Why have the authorities not intervened? Many mysteries remain. There are even reports that the current prime minister rode it before becoming well known. We will bring you further developments.

entries.en: Disaster Looters Here, Too
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k167; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Someone was seen rummaging through lockers in the workers' storeroom.
'Disaster looting' describes stealing other people's belongings amid the confusion of a fire.
There was no fire here, but taking advantage of the chaos of a catastrophe to rummage around amounts to the same thing.

Perhaps the person was searching for something necessary to survive the emergency. Witnesses, however, say their behavior suggested otherwise. Ever since being seen on the observation deck, they had wandered around excessively, seemingly doing nothing but looking for things to take.

The person has not been identified, and whether they subsequently survived is also unknown.
If they did make it out safely, I would like to hear what they were doing.

entries.en: Miyato Sky Tower in Ruins
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k169; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
We obtained footage of what used to be Miyato Sky Tower's second-floor observation deck.
Once bustling with families with children, and couples at night, it now bears no resemblance to its former self. All that remains is a horrifying scene of scattered rubble.

The second floor also had a lounge, a spot so famous that magazines once recommended it as an ideal place to propose.
Its popularity had declined somewhat as taller buildings and the restaurants on Sky Garden Bridge opened. But visitors had begun returning after a renovation about five years ago, making this all the more regrettable.

entries.en: Behind the Scenes at Work, Part 126
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k171; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Thanks to your support, this popular feature introducing workplaces we seldom see has reached its 126th installment.
This time, we report on the work of maintaining Miyato Sky Tower.

Miyato Sky Tower is repainted once every four years. This is not merely to keep it looking attractive. Preventing rust and repairing any rusty areas also keeps the tower safe and secure as well as beautiful.
Each repainting takes a year. Scaffolding is installed, but workers sometimes still have to move along narrow steel beams and paint by hand, making it extremely dangerous work.
Research into mechanization is progressing, but workers are also calling for it to stop, saying they cannot afford to lose their jobs.

entries.en:
Witness testimony revealed the presence of a man with extremely serious injuries.
Even to an amateur, his wounds reportedly looked unsurvivable.
Nevertheless, hoping to see his lover again, he fought desperately to stay conscious.
He was bleeding so heavily that he seemed likely to die at any moment.
Perhaps his powerful feelings for her were keeping him alive.

What happened to him afterward is unknown.
Hoping he was reunited safely with his lover, I intend to keep investigating.

entries.en: Heartless? Cruel? The Helicopter That Would Not Rescue Them
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k185; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Interviews with survivors revealed that many people stranded in Miyato Sky Tower had called for help from the rescue helicopter circling nearby.
Even with their voices hoarse and their arms so exhausted they could barely lift them, they reportedly waved and shouted for rescue.

Yet the rescue helicopter never began a rescue.
Of course, it repeatedly tried to do so. But wary of Gyaos, whose flying abilities far surpassed its own, it could not get close and was eventually shot down.

Hearing this afterward, one can understand that there was no choice. But for those on the observation deck, it also seems understandable that hope flickering before their eyes would leave them feeling abandoned.
According to a government announcement, discussions will be held on conducting future rescues with care for such emotional effects as well.

entries.en: A Door to Survival, or a Locked Gate to Hell
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k195; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
We now know that escape from Miyato Sky Tower's observation deck was delayed because the key to the emergency stairway door was temporarily lost and took time to find.

The worker carrying the key had fallen prey to Gyaos. There is no need to blame that itself. Rather, shouldn't preparations have been made for just such a possibility?
The simplest measure would be to keep a spare key elsewhere. Miyato Sky Tower had none, possessing only a single key. That will surely raise questions of responsibility.

Furthermore, sensors can now assess damage to buildings. I believe such equipment should be installed to unlock doors automatically when structural damage indicates that those stranded inside are in danger. Of course, power failures must also be considered, with independent generation such as solar cells on an emergency circuit.

In reality, discussions like this tend to stall at 'it costs money.' But once lives are lost, it is too late. With no telling what may happen or when, I believe doing everything possible to save lives is essential.

entries.en:
Birds' regurgitated matter is called pellets. Pellets from birds that prey on mice and similar animals contain fur and bones, so caution is needed: they may also contain pathogens from those animals.
Taking an interest is a good thing, but it is important to approach them with a full understanding of such dangers.

When collecting them, avoid touching them with your hands. After collection, sterilization in a microwave or similar appliance is necessary.

entries.en:
This footage captures a young person looking out from the damaged observation deck.
Were they contemplating the tragedy that might soon befall them, or resolving to return safely to the ground? We do not know what thoughts accompanied their view of the night skyline.
They were reportedly later seen running down the emergency stairs, but their survival has not been confirmed.

entries.en:
Have you heard the rumor about the men's restroom on Miyato Sky Tower's first-floor observation deck?
Every Christmas Eve at a particular time, a stall is occupied. Knock, and what sounds like the same man's voice answers, 'J-just a little longer...'
At first nobody paid attention. But after this continued for years, suspicious staff from the operating company used a stepladder that day to look over the stall and confirmed that nobody was inside.
They considered a prank involving a hidden microphone, but apparently found nothing of the sort, no matter how thoroughly they searched.
Unfortunately, I cannot reveal the time. There is also a rumor that those who give the exact time mysteriously disappear.
How much you believe is up to you.

entries.en: Miyato Sky Tower Rumors, Part 2
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k213; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
There is reportedly the following rumor about the women's restroom on Miyato Sky Tower's first-floor observation deck.
No particular season or time seems to be involved, but while looking in its mirror, you may suddenly see 'someone' standing behind you.
A woman who sees this then supposedly always feels 'someone' watching from somewhere, eventually suffering psychological damage.

One theory says it appears to women visiting on a date with a man of a certain appearance, though there is no proof.
If true, perhaps 'someone' has a powerful fixation on a man of that appearance and stalks the woman, unable to forgive her for being his girlfriend.

Whether it is a spirit is unknown.
How much you believe is up to you.

entries.en: Miyato Sky Tower Rumors, Part 3
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k215; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Little known to the public, Miyato Sky Tower's first-floor observation deck has a workers' storeroom.
With employee lockers and small supplies kept there, it has little to do with ordinary visitors.
But did you know a strange rumor surrounds it?

Very rarely, a high school girl is reportedly seen emerging from a locker in that storeroom.
Seeing her does not particularly bring misfortune, but the incident is so bizarre that many witnesses wonder if they hallucinated.

Is it a hallucination born of fantasy, or a real girl inside a locker for some reason?
How much you believe is up to you.

entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k217; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Many readers probably know this rumor about Miyato Sky Tower.
It is a sort of superstition: 'Visit on your third date, and you are certain to end up together.'

Despite speculation that the operating company invented it to attract visitors, many couples apparently did follow the advice and end up together.
Then again, those who broke up would rarely volunteer to talk about it, so perhaps that simply creates the impression.
How much you believe is up to you.

entries.en:
Did you know Miyato Sky Tower has rumors about studies as well as romance?
One says that praying for exam success on the observation deck while facing north-northwest on January 8 guarantees you will pass.
No actual statistics have been collected, but since the rumor spread, students and parents praying for success have formed lines there every year on that day.

In my own circle, about three people have made this 'pilgrimage to Miyato Sky Tower' over the past two or three years. Indeed, all passed the exams for their first choice.
On the other hand, another rumor says that praying toward the south-southeast that day brings misfortune, such as failed exams or unsuccessful job applications, to the person you picture while praying.
How much you believe is up to you.

entries.en:
Few people know that about five hundred years ago, row houses stood where Miyato Sky Tower is now.

Documents suggest their landlord was an ancestor of the man who would later own the inn.
Unlike his descendant, however, this landlord and his family were apparently respected for treating their tenants kindly.

On one occasion, he reportedly protected a tenant falsely accused of a crime and fought furiously against officials.
The landlord, his tenants, and townspeople who respected him barricaded themselves inside to confront the officials, while other townspeople investigated independently and found the true culprit. The landlord escaped punishment.

Amazingly, the magistrate at the time was so impressed by his character that he later sometimes sought the landlord's advice and assistance with difficult cases.
It is a harsh world when such an admirable person's descendant becomes a villain.

entries.en: This Land, Then and Now, Part 4
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k227; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
About fifteen hundred years ago, the site of today's Miyato Sky Tower was a market.

Most stalls consisted of cloth spread on the ground beneath simple roofs, lined up like stalls at a modern festival.
Although coins were being produced, they did not circulate widely among ordinary people, who generally bartered rice, cloth, and similar goods.

Perhaps because it was easily accessible, the market flourished, reportedly reaching as many as 954 stalls.
Amazingly, torches were lit here and there at night, allowing something like late-night business.

At some point, proper houses began replacing the simple stalls, and the market gradually changed into a town.

entries.en: This Land, Then and Now, Part 5
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k229; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Did you know that about three thousand years ago, a settlement stood where Miyato Sky Tower is today?
Its ruins were discovered underground during the tower's construction, even prompting a temporary campaign to change the construction site.

Investigations suggest a settlement of thirty or forty people, surrounded by almost obsessively extensive fencing. At its center stood a watchtower unusually tall for the period.

With no traces of contact with nearby settlements, it appears to have been isolated for some reason.
Perhaps its watchtower and sturdy fences reflected a life spent fearing attacks from outside.
Or perhaps it served something like a prison.
Unfortunately, the truth remains unknown.

entries.en: Broadcast Tower Trends: Projection Mapping
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k231; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Broadcast towers around the country are adopting various methods because their original appeal, simply seeing the view from high up, no longer attracts enough visitors.

Recently, projection mapping onto observation-deck floors and windows at night has begun to catch on.
Changing the designs with the seasons reportedly also helps bring visitors back.

Some towers have even begun projecting onto their exteriors.
Since projection mapping requires no alterations to the tower itself, its ease compared with older methods such as changing decorative lights may be another reason for its popularity.

entries.en: Broadcast Tower Trends: Moving Decorations
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k233; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Some broadcast towers deliberately use physical decorations to attract visitors.

One tower has decorations shaped like windmills, deer, and other things attached to it.
These not only light up but also move through various mechanisms.
Remarkably, changing the decorations by time of day as well as season allows it to cater to families, couples, and other visitors.
I doubt it pays for itself, but apparently a generous sponsor is involved.

entries.en: Broadcast Tower Trends: Transformation
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k235; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Did you know there are broadcast towers that transform?

Amazingly, one changes between five configurations according to the time of day and also changes its orientation with the seasons.
When I visited, I saw the third and fourth transformations. Frankly, I was impressed that such enormous movements were possible.
Its strength and structure reportedly exceed the required standards, so there is no problem. But it went so far that I wondered whether the transforming robots I watched as a child could be built, too.

The transformations were so smooth that even from the observation deck, one would hardly expect motion sickness or discomfort. It was extremely enjoyable.
I recommend visiting at least once.

entries.en: Broadcast Tower Trends: Raa-ko
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k237; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
There is a broadcast tower with an enormous mascot clinging to it.
Raa-ko, the tower's cuddly local mascot, is hanging onto the structure.
It is so large that even from far away, you can tell 'something' is attached to the tower.

Amazingly, Raa-ko moves up and down the tower.
It makes the journey every hour, and when it reaches the top, a sound announces the time.

Cute mascot or not, its enormous face seen from the observation deck reportedly frightens some children into tears.
Personally, though, I was quietly impressed by the technology: its precisely timed journeys and the near absence of motor noise while it moves.

entries.en: Broadcast Tower Trends: Growth
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0064.json:p0/k239; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Did you know there is a broadcast tower that grows?

It gets a little taller every year.
Of course, it does not grow naturally like bamboo.
Put simply, each year it is rebuilt at an unbelievable speed to make it taller.

And as the tower grows taller, it needs more land. That is why the surrounding properties are being purchased one by one.
Now more than 530 meters tall, this broadcast tower reportedly intends to keep growing.
Perhaps one day we will gaze upon Earth from an observation deck beyond the stratosphere.
